sights.address: 24 Chánh Hưng, Ward 4, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A near-180-year-old Buddhist temple in District 8 whose surfaces are almost entirely mosaicked in over 30 tonnes of broken porcelain and ceramic shards — bowls, plates, teapots — applied by hand from 1961 to 2004. Holds a Vietnam Book of Records mark for the most ceramic pieces, plus a pair of 3.4 m, 1.8-tonne candles. The 'Miểng Sành' pagoda is District 8's signature sight.

sights.address: Cù lao Bà Tàng, Ward 7, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A communal house of more than 150 years standing alone on a two-hectare islet in the Kênh Đôi canal, granted a royal decree by Emperor Tự Đức in 1853 and ranked a national historic-cultural relic. Reached by a short ferry hop, it is a highlight of District 8's on-the-water heritage tours — a rare Nam Bộ đình marooned mid-canal.

sights.n: Bến Bình Đông & the Tết Flower Market
sights.address: Bến Bình Đông (along Kênh Tàu Hủ), Ward 11, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The old rice-trade wharf strung along Kênh Tàu Hủ, once the 'prosperous Tàu Hủ avenue' linking Saigon-Chợ Lớn to the Mekong. Each Lunar New Year it becomes the 'trên bến dưới thuyền' flower market, with growers selling blooms straight off sampans — the most atmospheric Tết scene in the city and a working glimpse of canal-borne Saigon.

sights.address: Nguyễn Văn Linh, Ward 7, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The largest wholesale market in Vietnam, a 65-hectare complex in far-southwest District 8 and the biggest seafood distribution hub in the south. It runs through the night — hundreds of tonnes of fish, produce and flowers moving from about 1am to 11am. Not a polished tourist stop but an extraordinary look at how the city is fed.

sights.address: Đỗ Năng Tế, Bình Trị Đông A Ward, Bình Tân, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: One of Saigon's oldest temples and the flagship Buddhist sight of Bình Tân, famed for extraordinary woodwork: ironwood doors carved with the 12 zodiac animals and eight vajra guardians (a Vietnam record), and giant fragrant-wood Buddhas including a 16-tonne, 8 m Amitabha billed as the tallest wooden Buddha statue in the country.

sights.address: Cầu Nhị Thiên Đường (over Kênh Đôi), Ward 5, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A 1925 bridge over the Kênh Đôi, said to be the first reinforced-concrete bridge in Indochina, built by the Chinese-Vietnamese magnate behind the Nhị Thiên Đường medicated-oil empire. A row of arches beneath it evokes an old Roman viaduct; a District 8 landmark and marker of the Nam Bộ resistance era.

sights.address: 1 Đường số 17A, Bình Trị Đông B Ward, Bình Tân, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The 114,000 sqm Japanese-run mall that anchors Bình Tân, opened 2016 as one of the largest in Ho Chi Minh City — cinema, a huge food street, and the everyday air-conditioned pull for the district's working-class west. The practical family day-out landmark out here.

sights.address: Chợ Xóm Củi, Ward 10, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A decades-old District 8 market whose name ('firewood hamlet') recalls the canal-side firewood depots that once supplied Chợ Lớn. It grew from those wood yards into the district's central market of hundreds of stalls — a dense, cheap street-food warren and a window on working-class Rạch Ông life.
